title.narrative: Building Adaptive Capacity and Resilience of Pastoral and Agro-pastoral Communities to Climate Shocks in Somali region of Ethiopia

description.narrative: This project aims to pilot the roll out of the Transhumance Tracking Tool (TTT) in Dollo and Shabelle Zones of Somali region, Ethiopia, to strengthen the evidence base of life-saving humanitarian action while enhancing the adaptive capacities and resilience of pastoral and agro-pastoral communities affected by climate shocks and stresses. The piloting of the TTT system in drought and flood-prone woredas of Somali region will involve initial primary and secondary research to identify convergence zones to set up Pastoral Mobility Tracking Points (PMTP) (Phase 1), establishment of a Pastoral Flow Monitoring Network (Phase 2), data collection and analysis on herder flows, weather, conflict and route accessibility (Phase 3), and then interpretation and visualization data publication (Phase 4). The TTT system will use available data – including historical local knowledge – to profile, predict and identify locations where pastoralists are likely to move in case of shocks. Data produced by the TTT will directly inform the complementary response of FAO under this CERF allocation, ensuring that strong and effective localized risk- informed early warning system is integrated into the broader response to plan in anticipation of and address the immediate needs of the targeted communities. This analysis will inform the establishment of water points for livestock by FAO under this CERF allocation, leading to evidence-based provision of livestock water to strengthen contributing towards climate change adaptation and resilience. In addition, IOM will support climate resilient agricultural practices. The project will ultimately support the most vulnerable households in the selected woredas through risk-informed and climate smart life-saving assistance, to enabling them to safeguard and restore their livelihoods and adapt to climate shocks for improved food security, nutrition and income generation. Moreover, in the presence of these established systems, the TTT data will feed into the analysis of strategic hotspots to anticipate normal to significantly elevated pastoralist movements utilizing a vulnerability index from concurrent climate extremes. This approach will enhance coordination, strengthen synergies and ensure that response packages are designed based on evidence and needs, thus fulfilling immediate humanitarian needs while promoting early action that can benefit the overall humanitarian response.
